tasks.short: Coordinate front office activities and resolve problems.

steps.what: Read front office activities for today.
Coordinate front office activities with housekeeping.
Hear front office problems at the desk.
Decide how to resolve front office problems.
Review the drafted status of front office problems.

loop.input: The problem the manager logged and the decision the manager already made
loop.output: A status line that uses only that log and that decision
loop.check: The lodging manager rejects any cause that is not in the log
loop.stop: One draft, at most 80 words. Gaps stay blank. No second pass.
loop.why_not_simpler: Desk problems are free text, so a fixed status cannot open from the words used

steps.what: File the approved status for front office problems.

tasks.design: The lodging manager still coordinates the front office and decides each problem. A status is drafted only from the log and that decision, then checked. {WORKFLOW} files the accepted status. Coordination calls stay calls.
tasks.previous_blocker: The day's problems and the coordination sat in calls and were typed up later.
tasks.enabler_now: The stay list is already on the property system. The status can be filed once the manager has accepted it.
tasks.still_hard: Solving a desk problem still depends on the people and the guest involved.
tasks.human_edge: The manager coordinates the desk and decides the problem. The file is a record of that decision.
tasks.altitude: Coordination and problem solving stay in the day. Writing the status after the decision gets shorter.

reach.task: Sort a desk problem during the shift
reach.learn: Log the problem before asking the manager to decide it

evidence.claim: A status line can be drafted from a problem someone has already logged and decided.

assumptions: The status stores the stay or desk reference, the facts the manager logged, and the decision. The manager produces the decision. Calls are not transcribed.
The workflow starts with the day's activity list and ends when the accepted status is filed. It does not move staff between roles.
The prior classes this as amplify. The steps keep coordination and the decision human, and only the status wording is drafted.
Upkeep is the problem categories on the register.
unknowns: Whether front-office problems are already a queue someone else owns.
Whether coordination with housekeeping is a meeting or a short call.
research_questions: Where are front-office problems written down today?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the problem status is already in that step

approvals.approved_version: front office problem status the lodging manager accepted after hearing the problem

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Coordination and the decision remain. Filing an accepted status is the saving. The range sits under the central net and is not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect guest rooms, public areas, and grounds.

steps.what: Inspect guest rooms, public areas and grounds.
Judge cleanliness after you inspect guest rooms.
Review the cleanliness note from the grounds inspection.

loop.input: Notes written during the inspection and the decision made after it
loop.output: A cleanliness note that names only rooms and grounds on those notes
loop.check: The lodging manager rejects any room they did not inspect
loop.stop: One draft. Rooms without a note stay off the list. No second pass.
loop.why_not_simpler: Inspection notes are free text from a walk, so a fixed line cannot know what was seen

steps.what: Send the approved cleanliness note to housekeeping.

tasks.design: The lodging manager inspects the rooms, the public areas and the grounds, then decides what is not acceptable. A note is drafted only from that inspection and checked before {WORKFLOW} sends it to housekeeping. The send happens after the inspection.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings were written on a pad during the walk and copied into a message afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Once the manager has accepted the note from the walk, sending it is a record.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing cleanliness and appearance still requires the person in the room and on the grounds.
tasks.human_edge: The manager's eyes decide what is clean enough. The note cannot add a room.
tasks.altitude: The inspection round stays the bulk of the task. Copying the accepted findings to housekeeping gets shorter.

reach.task: Assign rooms to clean after an inspection
reach.learn: Act on the note from the inspection, and do not treat it as a new standard

evidence.claim: An inspection note can repeat what a person wrote on the walk, after that person accepts it.

assumptions: The note stores the room or area, the finding from the walk, and the decision made after the inspection. The manager produces the decision. Cameras are not a source.
The approval is the review of the note after the inspection. It does not happen from a desk list written before the walk.
The prior classes this as human. The steps agree. The inspection stays at full time and is most of the task.
Upkeep is the room and area names.
unknowns: How many rooms the manager inspects personally, against a sample.
Whether housekeeping already records the same findings on a device during the walk.
research_questions: Is the inspection a full round or a sample of rooms?

already_counted.description: Checking the note against the walk is already in the review step

incremental.description: Keep room and area names on the note

approvals.approved_version: cleanliness note the lodging manager accepted after inspecting the rooms and grounds

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The inspection stays at full time. Only the accepted note is sent without retyping. The range sits under the central net and is not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign duties and schedule shifts from working-time rules.

steps.what: Set constraints before you schedule shifts.
Schedule shifts from the working-time constraints.
Accept the draft before duties are assigned.
Assign duties on the accepted shift roster.
Publish the accepted roster that schedules shifts.

tasks.design: The lodging manager sets the working-time constraints. A configured solver on {HCM} drafts the shifts from those constraints only. The manager accepts the roster and assigns duties. {HCM} publishes that accepted roster. There is no model and no behaviour score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shifts were built on a sheet because the constraints lived in people's heads and in mail.
tasks.enabler_now: A scheduler can apply hours limits the manager has already entered. Publishing can wait for acceptance.
tasks.still_hard: Assigning who does which duty, and accepting the roster, stay with the manager. National working-time rules still have to be the constraints.
tasks.human_edge: The manager owns the constraints, the acceptance and the duties. The solver only arranges hours inside those constraints.
tasks.altitude: Building the grid of shifts gets shorter. The manager still sets the rules, accepts the roster and assigns duties before anyone sees it.

reach.task: Set the desk rota for the week
reach.learn: Publish a roster only after the same acceptance, using hours constraints and not a score

evidence.claim: Shift planning from stated hours constraints is a configured solver. It does not need a model.
Publishing a roster of named staff can require works-council consent under national rules. A roster must not score behaviour or traits.

assumptions: The solver inputs are the hours limits, the roles and the leave the manager entered. It does not read performance, behaviour or traits. The manager produces the constraints and the acceptance.
The publish step files the roster version the manager accepted, including the duties the manager assigned. It does not publish the untouched draft.
The task is labelled automate. The steps agree that the grid can be configured, and they disagree that duties and acceptance can be left to the solver.
National rules on working time are constraints the customer must confirm. Consent days cover a works-council check before a roster tool is used.
Upkeep is keeping the hours limits and the role list current.
unknowns: Whether a works council must consent before this roster is published.
Which collective or statutory hours limits apply at this site.
Whether a scheduler is already in use, in which case the draft step is existing system time and the saving shrinks.
research_questions: Is a shift solver already publishing rosters, or is the roster still a sheet?

already_counted.description: Accepting the roster and assigning duties stay in those steps

incremental.description: Keep hours limits and roles current on the scheduler

approvals.approved_version: shift roster the lodging manager accepted before it was published

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The draft grid can be configured. Acceptance, duties and the existing rules stay human. If a solver already publishes the roster, that time is not a new saving. The range sits under the central net and is not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take registration payments, confirm stays, or return checks.

steps.what: Receive advance registration payments from the guest.
Process and record registration payments already counted.
Decide if registrations can be accepted.
Review confirmation letters for accepted registrations.
Mail the approved confirmation letters.
Return checks when registrations cannot be accepted.
File the refusal when registrations cannot be accepted.

tasks.design: The lodging manager counts the advance payment and decides whether the registration can be accepted. {OPS_SYSTEM} records the counted amount and, if accepted, fills a confirmation from the booking fields. The manager checks that letter before {EMAIL} sends it. Returning a check stays with the manager. A refusal is filed only after the decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payments, letters and returned checks were each typed or written by hand from the same booking.
tasks.enabler_now: The booking fields can fill a confirmation. Sending it can wait until the manager has checked that version.
tasks.still_hard: Accepting or refusing a registration, and handing a check back, stay with the manager.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides acceptance and handles the check. The letter is only the booking fields they already accepted.
tasks.altitude: Counting money, deciding acceptance and returning checks stay. The confirmation is no longer retyped, and it goes out only after the manager checks it.

reach.task: Send a confirmation for a booking the desk accepted
reach.learn: Send the letter version a person checked, and do not send a refusal by itself

evidence.claim: A confirmation can be filled from booking fields a person has already accepted, then sent only after that person checks the letter.
Returning a payment when a registration is refused is handled by a person.

assumptions: The payment record stores the amount the manager counted, the reservation id and the tender type. The manager produces the count and the acceptance. A card authorisation that already succeeded in the property system is not re-counted as human time.
The confirmation letter uses the guest name, dates, room and amount from the accepted booking. The manager checks that version before it is mailed. The mail step references that checked version.
The refusal file references the same acceptance decision. Returning the check is a separate human action and is not mailed by the system.
The workflow ends at the sent confirmation or the returned check. It does not set a rate.
Upkeep is the letter fields and the payment field map.
unknowns: Whether advance payments already post from the card device without a second entry.
Who may refuse a registration, and whether a returned check needs a second signature.
research_questions: Which payment types are already posted by the property system?

already_counted.description: Checking the confirmation letter is already in the review step

incremental.description: Keep confirmation fields and payment types current

approvals.approved_version: payment amount the lodging manager counted before it was recorded
confirmation letter the lodging manager checked for this accepted registration
refusal the lodging manager decided for this registration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Counting, acceptance and returning checks remain. Recording a counted amount and mailing a checked letter are the saving. The range sits under the central net and is not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Desk coordination, room inspections and payment decisions stay. Shift grids and accepted statuses take less retyping. The roster is published only after the manager accepts it.
reach: Housekeeping acts on a cleanliness note written after the inspection
The desk sends a confirmation only in the version the manager checked
skills_to_grow: Setting working-time constraints before a roster is drafted
Accepting a roster before it is published
Refusing a registration without sending a confirmation
role.ambitious_version: Each published roster is one the manager accepted, and each confirmation matches a registration the manager accepted.
